title: Revoke unlimited allowances — the #1 wallet heist vector
body: Every `approve(token, spender, uint256.max)` you signed lets that spender drain the full token balance at any moment. Uniswap routers, bridges and 90% of dapps request them. Revoke anything you no longer use weekly (revoke.cash, etherscan token-approval checker, or a local script). Check your nonce-0 approval grants first — those never expire.
command: chain-scout: run app.py, open the Approvals tab, revoke every 'dangerous' row

title: An EOA spender with an allowance is a standing risk
body: Allowances should go to contracts, never to plain EOAs. A wallet that approved an EOA can have its balance pulled by a private key you don't control. Chain-scout flags any allowance whose spender has no code. If you ever see one in your own wallet, revoke it before you touch any other dapp.
command: python -c 'from chain_scout.heuristics import classify_approval; ...'

title: Airdrops are the bait, approvals are the hook
body: Dust and 'free' airdrops arrive from brand-new contracts precisely so you'll click: check the token page -> 'Approve to swap' -> sign a max-uint approval -> the airdrop contract or its 'migrate' frontend drains your real tokens. Treat any airdrop of a token you never bought as hostile until proven otherwise.
command: chain-scout: the Inbound tab labels unknown-sender transfers

title: Meme tokens with tiny holder counts are rug bait
body: A token with <2,500 holders, sub-$0.01 price and a top-10 concentration over 60% is statistically a pump-and-dump vehicle. You can't sell what nobody will buy — exit liquidity is the rug. Chain-scout's rug heuristics flag exactly this shape (holder proxy + concentration bands + liquidity ratio).
command: chain-scout: RUGX demo token shows score 0.76 for this pattern

title: Market cap vs liquidity: the 10x rule
body: If a token's market cap is more than ~10x its DEX liquidity, even a successful small exit crashes the price — the classic soft-rug. A 20x+ ratio means the 'value' only exists on paper. Chain-scout computes mcap/liquidity per token when the data is available and scores the ratio into the token rug score.
command: chain-scout: rug flag reason text shows the exact ratio band

title: AI phishing is now fully automated — verify before you sign
body: LLMs generate perfect fake dapp frontends, support chats and wallet-connect popups in seconds. The rule is unchanged: never sign a blind signature, never approve max-uint from a link in a DM, and always confirm the domain of the site that opened the signing window. 'The AI said it's fine' is not a security control.
command: bookmark only: your wallet's phishing list + chain-scout for leftovers

title: Testnet-first: scan Sepolia before you touch mainnet
body: Every scanner feature can be exercised on Sepolia with faucet tokens and zero financial risk. Chain-scout defaults to Sepolia for live scans; mainnet requires MAINNET_ALLOWED=1. Demo habits on testnets, then apply the same discipline on mainnet.
command: MAINNET_ALLOWED=1 streamlit run app.py   # only when you mean it

title: Holder concentration is the single best on-chain rug predictor
body: Top-10 holder share of a token supply tells you who can dump at will. 90%+ concentration = the team wallet is the market. Keyless APIs rarely expose top-10 lists, so chain-scout uses a holders-count proxy when needed — and always labels which source it used, so you know the confidence of the signal.
command: chain-scout: concentration_signal() bands in heuristics.py

title: Dead tokens are free money for phishers
body: A token with no transfers in 30 days is 'dead' — yet it still shows a balance and a fake 'swap' button somewhere. Chain-scout scores dead tokens into rug exposure and dust exposure, because dead balances are precisely what phishing sites drain after a fresh approval.
command: chain-scout: dead_signal() window = 30 days

title: Your cost basis is not public — PnL tools must say so
body: Anyone claiming exact PnL from an address alone is guessing: cost basis lives off-chain (exchanges, wallets, tax records). Chain-scout only reports PnL where an entry price exists (demo wallets carry clearly-labeled demo entries); everything else is value-only. Treat 'AI PnL estimates' as entertainment, not tax advice.
command: chain-scout: estimate_pnl() skips tokens without basis

title: Whitelist your exchanges in the phishing scan
body: Inbound transfers from Binance/Coinbase hot wallets are normal activity; transfers from random EOA contracts are the airdrop-bait pattern. Chain-scout ships a small trusted-sender set (add your own via the fixture) and scores the share of unknown-sender inbound transfers in the last 30 days.
command: chain-scout: trust_senders in fixtures/demo_wallet.json

title: Decimals lie: check the token contract, not the label
body: A token with 6 decimals displays 1,000,000 units where one with 18 decimals shows 1,000,000,000,000,000,000 units of the same 'amount'. Scanners that ignore decimals produce fantasy valuations. Chain-scout always converts raw balances through the token's declared decimals before pricing.
command: chain-scout: TokenHolding.decimals drives all value math

title: Unlimited approval to a known router is still a risk
body: Infinite allowances to Uniswap/SushiSwap routers can't be drained by the router code today — but router upgrades, governance attacks and exploit chains make 'known and safe' a status that decays. Chain-scout downgrades router approvals to 'watch' and tells you to right-size them when convenient.
command: chain-scout: classify_approval() router branch -> 'watch'

title: Rainbow-phishing uses NFT approvals, not just ERC-20
body: setApprovalForAll is the ERC-721/1155 cousin of approve(): one signature and a marketplace contract can move every NFT you own. Chain-scout currently covers ERC-20; treat setApprovalForAll grants with the same paranoia and revoke them at the same cadence.
command: revoke.cash covers both token standards

title: A high risk score is a warning, not a verdict
body: Risk scores aggregate public-data signals and miss everything off-chain (who controls the deployer key, what the team is doing, regulatory status). Chain-scout's report always says so, and the score formula is printed inside the app — read it before you act on it.
command: chain-scout: 'How the score works' expander in app.py

title: Multichain wallets need per-chain scans
body: An approval on Ethereum says nothing about your Arbitrum or Polygon exposure: allowances are per-chain, per-token, per-spender. Chain-scout is Ethereum-first (Sepolia default) — add RPC endpoints for other chains and re-run the same heuristics per chain.
command: CHAIN_SCOUT_RPC_URL=https://… any chain's public RPC

title: Beware the 'verification' fake: verified code ≠ safe code
body: Scam tokens get their source verified on explorers too — verification only proves the deployed bytecode matches some source, not that the source is honest (hidden mint functions, blacklisted-router tax, owner-only transfers all verify fine). Don't let a green 'verified' checkmark replace your own flag checks.
command: chain-scout: treat holder/liquidity signals as primary, verified flag as noise

title: Keyless scanners are reproducible scanners
body: If a scanner needs your private API key, its results cannot be independently re-run — and 'trust me, I have the key' is exactly how scam tools operate. Chain-scout runs keyless (public RPC, free CoinGecko tier, bundled fixtures) so anyone can verify any report. Same logic applies to the tools you use.
command: python scripts/fetch_fixtures.py   # rebuilds the demo data

title: Fast-blockchain scams are faster — check time-to-rug
body: On chains with 2s blocks, a 'liquidity added, then removed within an hour' pattern is a rug you can watch in real time. For any token you buy on a fast chain, snapshot liquidity and top-10 holders when you enter, and diff them a week later. Chain-scout's fixture format makes such snapshots easy to persist.
command: chain-scout: run the scanner weekly, diff token_rug scores

title: The permission triage: revoke / reduce / keep
body: For every approval you find, pick a bucket: revoke now (EOA spender, known-bad, unlimited-on-unknown), reduce to a usable exact amount (routers you use monthly), keep only for actively-used core dapps. A monthly 10-minute triage removes 90% of wallet-drain surface.
command: chain-scout: Approvals tab verdicts sort straight into these buckets

title: Simulate before you sign — the free safety net
body: Tenderly Simulation, Fire (formerly Flashbots Protect), and wallet 'transaction preview' features execute a tx against a copy of chain state and show you the exact token deltas — before any gas is spent. Use them for anything an AI assistant suggested; simulations beat reading code for catching value-extraction tricks.
command: tenderly.co simulation of any approval/spend tx

title: Your scanner is only as good as its data freshness
body: Token prices, holder counts and approvals decay in hours. A report that says 'looks fine' from last week is a lie this week. Chain-scout stamps every snapshot with its timestamp and marks fixtures as static demo data — always check the stamp before trusting a cached report.
command: chain-scout: snapshot_ts in fixture meta + data_source label
